obtained.how: full text not obtained; secondary only: Harris (2006, Virginia Tech MS thesis, already fetched for the pass as Harris_2006) restates one of the article's findings

claims.claim: in Oneida, young white perch took 2–12 times more prey biomass per gram than young yellow perch in 1980, and their growth tracked late-summer D. pulex (abstract only)
claims.note: Neither the article nor its abstract could be read; Harris 2006 says only that trophic overlap between age-0 yellow perch and white perch in Oneida was significant (> 0.6) (Harris p. 3, PDF p. 15).

claims.claim: amphipods and chironomids from ~40 mm (Prout, Mills & Forney 1990, via Harris 2006)
claims.note: Harris 2006, p. 6 (PDF p. 18), says a diet shift 'at 40 mm TL (from copepods and daphnids to amphipods and chironomids)' was documented in age-0 white perch in Oneida Lake (Prout et al. 1990). The secondary citation is faithfully relayed (40 mm TOTAL length), but the article itself was not read.

claims.claim: in 1987, when D. pulex vanished, young white and yellow perch switched to bed invertebrates and grew more slowly (abstract)
claims.note: Not read; Harris 2006 does not mention 1987.
